Below is a 12‑week strength program starting Monday, 2026‑06‑01. It’s periodized around a regular 28‑day cycle with severe primary dysmenorrhea on flow days 1–3. On flow days 1–3 there is: no high intensity, no heavy Valsalva/bracing, no jumping. Outside the flow window she’s fully cleared.

Assumptions and structure
- Cycle pattern from last known period: LMP 2026‑05‑01; regular 28 days. Projected menses start dates during the plan:
  - 2026‑05‑29 (prior to program start; ends ~05‑31)
  - 2026‑06‑26 (flow days ~06‑26 to 06‑28)
  - 2026‑07‑24 (flow days ~07‑24 to 07‑26)
  - 2026‑08‑21 (flow days ~08‑21 to 08‑23)
- Training week runs Mon–Sun. Strength days 3×/week plus 1 GPP/conditioning day. During flow days 1–3, we pivot to deload/recovery sessions with light loads, no valsalva, no jumping. If a flow day falls on a scheduled hard day, we swap in the recovery protocol and shift the harder session later in the week where possible.
- Phasing
  - Weeks 1–4: Base/Hypertrophy (technique density, 3–4 sets of 6–12, RPE 6–8)
  - Weeks 5–8: Strength (lower reps, higher load, RPE 7–9 on non-flow weeks; taper during flow)
  - Weeks 9–12: Peak & Consolidate (top sets at RPE 8–9 outside flow; strategic deloads on flow weeks; finalize with rep‑PRs submax)

Global guidelines
- Warm‑up every session: 5–8 min easy cyc, row or walk; dynamic mobility (hips, T‑spine, ankles, shoulders); 2–3 ramp sets for main lift.
- Bracing/breathing: Outside flow window, cue diaphragmatic brace as appropriate. On flow days 1–3, avoid prolonged breath holds; use continuous breathing cadence.
- Tempo notation if used: e.g., 3‑0‑1 means 3s eccentric, no pause, 1s up.
- RPE: 6 “could do 4 reps more,” 7 “3 reps in reserve,” 8 “2 RIR,” 9 “1 RIR.”

Flow‑safe substitutions and rules
- On flow days 1–3: replace jumps, sprints, heavy bracing, and high‑intensity intervals with:
  - Mobility, cyc/elliptical walk, breathing, light band/cable work, isometrics at low intensity, machine/goblet variations under RPE 5–6.

Core daily targets (baseline across the month)
- Energy: match to goal (maintenance or modest deficit/surplus). If training feels flat in follicular/ovulatory weeks, increase carbs 10–15% on lift days.

Supplements (confirm with GP; verify no interactions)
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g daily.

Menstrual phase (Flow days 1–3: severe cramps; days 4–5 if lingering)
Goals: anti‑inflammatory focus, gentle on GI, maintain energy with easy‑to‑digest foods; support iron and hydration.

  - Protein: keep baseline; lean, tender options (eggs, yogurt, fish, tofu).

  - Fats: include omega‑3s (salmon, sardines, chia, walnuts) and olive oil; keep saturated fats lower.

- If cramps or GI symptoms spike with certain foods (e.g., very spicy, high‑fat fried foods), scale them back during late luteal/flow.
- If fatigue persists despite sleep and nutrition, discuss ferritin, vitamin D, B12 with GP.
- Track symptoms with food/training log to personalize triggers and winners across two cycles.

  - Mobility 10–15 min

  - Breathing/relaxation 5–10 min

Optional Post-Phase Testing Week (Aug 24–30) — After flow
- Mon Aug 24: Squat 1RM test (ramp: 5@50%, 3@60%, 2@70%, 1@80%, 1@85%, then ~90%, ~95%, attempt 1RM). Optional back-off 1–2×3 @ ~85% if fresh.
- Wed Aug 26: Bench 1RM (similar ramp). Optional 1–2×3 @ ~85%.
- Fri Aug 28: Deadlift 1RM (ramp: 3–4@50%, 2@60–70%, 1@80%, 1@88–90%, ~94–95%, attempt 1RM).

Aerobic base summary (integrated with above)
- Zone 2 sessions progress Tue/Sat from 30–35 min up to 60–70 min by Week 10; Thursday HIIT replaces the prior “tempo” prescription.
- During flow days 1–3: all cardio becomes Z1–2 easy (15–30 min), walking or bike; no HIIT, no plyos.

HIIT summary (Thu each week; removed/modified during flow)
- Weeks 1–4: progress 8×30 s to 6–8×40 s; deload if PMS.
- Weeks 5–8: 8–10×45 s; one mixed 60 s set in Week 7; moderate in Week 8 pre-flow.
- Weeks 9–12: 8–10×60 s (or 6×75 s in Week 10), then taper Weeks 11–12.

Plyometric/Power day summary (Tue; no jumping on flow days 1–3)
- Weeks 1–4: elastic prep, med-ball throws, box/broad jumps to stick; taper Week 4 pre-flow.
- Weeks 5–8: add hang high-pulls or heavier med-ball; hurdle hops; bounds; front-load Week 8 pre-flow.
- Weeks 9–12: maintain sharpness; introduce gentle reactive pairings; light pre-flow in Week 12.

Nutrition plan (cycle-aware, concise)
- Baseline daily: protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg; carbs 3–5 g/kg (4–6 g/kg on hard lift days in follicular/ovulatory); fats 0.8–1.0 g/kg; fiber 25–35 g; fluids 30–40 ml/kg + 500–1000 ml around training; electrolytes as needed.
- Supplements (confirm with GP): creatine 3–5 g/day; omega-3 (EPA/DHA) 1–2 g/day; magnesium glycinate 200–400 mg PM; vitamin D3 1000–2000 IU if needed; iron only if deficient; ginger 1–2 g/day and curcumin 500–1000 mg/day during late luteal/flow if tolerated.
- Menstrual phase (Flow days 1–3): easy-to-digest carbs (oats, rice, ripe fruit), lean proteins (eggs, yogurt, tofu, fish), omega-3s, iron + vitamin C pairing; smaller, more frequent meals; broths/herbal teas; avoid very gassy foods if bloated.
- Early–mid follicular: push carbs around training (pre 30–60 g; post 0.6–0.8 g/kg + 25–40 g protein); varied colorful foods.
- Luteal: stabilize energy; slightly lower carbs 3–4 g/kg unless training heavy; keep protein high; manage cravings with planned snacks; steady electrolytes; 2–3 servings calcium (or fortified alt); limit late caffeine; magnesium for sleep.
- Peri-workout (all phases): if >75–90 min sessions, consider 20–30 g carbs every 30–40 min; post 25–40 g protein + carbs.

Recovery and symptom management
- Sleep 7–9 h; consistent schedule. Add 30–60 min during late luteal/flow if fatigued.
- Heat therapy post-session during flow; light mobility helps.
- Strictly avoid Valsalva and jumping on flow days 1–3; use exhale-through-effort and lighter loads.
- Auto-regulate with RPE; if cramps/fatigue elevate RPE, reduce load/sets and favor machines.
- Track symptoms and adjust week-to-week; don’t “make up” missed volume—resume plan.

This plan delivers a complete, cycle-aware 12-week build with high-intensity strength in Phase 2, aerobic base, HIIT, and power work, while protecting her during flow windows and setting up an optional post-flow 1RM testing week.

Here’s the complete 12-week program starting Monday, 2026-06-01, with all adjustments integrated: cycle-aware strength (with a higher-intensity Phase 2), aerobic base, weekly HIIT, a Tuesday plyometric/power day, flow-day modifications, nutrition, and an optional post-flow 1RM test week.

Cycle planning and constraints
- Regular 28-day cycle; severe dysmenorrhea on flow days 1–3.
- Projected menses during plan: Jun 26–28, Jul 24–26, Aug 21–23.
- Flow days 1–3 rules: no high-intensity, no heavy Valsalva/bracing, no jumping. Sessions those days convert to Flow-Safe Recovery or Flow-Safe Power/HIIT alternatives.

Weekly training template (outside flow)
- Mon: Lower A (squat focus) + short Z2 flush optional
- Tue: Power/Plyometrics day + Zone 2 steady aerobic session (can stack if time allows; do power first), or split to Tue/Wed AM/PM
- Wed: Upper A + optional 10–15 min Z2 flush
- Thu: HIIT (replaces tempo from aerobic plan on that day)
- Fri: Lower B (hinge focus) + optional 10–15 min Z2 flush
- Sat: Long Zone 2 aerobic session (combine with GPP sled/carries some weeks)
- Sun: Off or easy walk/mobility; during flow this is the main movement

Intensity guidance
- RPE: 6–8 in Phase 1, 8–9 peaks in Phase 2 (non-flow), 7–8 in Phase 3. Auto-regulate: if a day moves +1 RPE over plan, reduce load 5–10% or drop a set.

PHASE 1: Weeks 1–4 (Jun 1–Jun 28) — Base and Hypertrophy

Week 1 (Jun 1–7) — No flow
- Mon Lower A

  - DB RDL: 3×10 @ RPE 7
  - Leg press: 2×12 @ RPE 7

- Tue Power + Zone 2
  - Warm-up: 5–8 min easy + mobility
  - Low-level plyos: ankle pogos 3×20; line hops fwd/back 2×20; snap downs 3×5

  - Contrast: trap-bar jump shrug 3×4 @ 20–30% BW

- Wed Upper A

- Thu HIIT

  - Optional Z2 flush: 10 min
- Sat Long Zone 2 + GPP
  - Z2: 35 min easy bike/walk
  - GPP (optional): Sled push light 6×20–30 m; farmer carry 4×30–40 m; 10 min mobility
- Sun: 20–30 min easy walk + mobility

Week 2 (Jun 8–14)
- Mon Lower A: Back squat 4×6 @ RPE 7–8; RFESS 3×9/side; DB RDL 3×10; Leg press 3×10–12; Copenhagen plank (knees) 3×20–30 s/side; 10 min Z2 optional

- Thu HIIT: 8×40 s hard / 80 s easy

  - 10×45 s hard / 75 s easy

  - Hip thrust 3×5 @ RPE 8–9
  - Step-up 3×8/side
  - Ham curl 3×8–10
  - Dead bug 3×10/side
- Sat Long Zone 2: 55 min
- Sun: Easy walk/mobility

Week 7 (Jul 13–19)

  - Secondary: low-mod hurdle hops 5×3; broad jump 4×2 (stick)

  - Arms 2–3×8–12

  - 6×60 s hard (RPE 8.5–9) / 120 s easy + 4×30 s hard / 60 s easy
- Fri Lower B
  - Deadlift 1×2 @ RPE 9, then 3×2 @ −3–5%
  - Hip thrust 3×4–5 @ RPE 9 (crisp reps, no grind)

  - Ham curl 3×8–10

Week 8 (Jul 20–26) — Flow expected Fri–Sun (Jul 24–26). Push early; deload during flow.
- Mon Lower A (last heavy squat)
  - Back squat 1×2–3 @ RPE 9, then 2×2–3 @ −3–5%
  - RFESS 2×6–8/side @ RPE 7–8
  - BB RDL 2×5–6 @ RPE 7–8

  - Jump squat 2×3
  - Zone 2: 50–55 min

  - Bench 1×2–3 @ RPE 9, then 2×2–3 @ −3–5%

  - Incline DB press 2×6–8 @ RPE 7–8
  - Lat pulldown 2×8–10

  - 6–8×45 s hard / 90 s easy, or swap to 20–25 min Z1–2 if PMS rising

  - 15–25 min easy cycle or gentle walk

  - Light machine leg press or goblet squat 2–3×12–15 @ RPE ≤6

Week 10 (Aug 3–9) — Slight overload

- Weeks 9–12: maintain sharpness; introduce gentle reactive pairings; light pre-flow in Week 12.

Nutrition plan (cycle-aware, concise)
- Baseline daily: protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg; carbs 3–5 g/kg (4–6 g/kg on hard lift days in follicular/ovulatory); fats 0.8–1.0 g/kg; fiber 25–35 g; fluids 30–40 ml/kg + 500–1000 ml around training; electrolytes as needed.
- Supplements (confirm with GP): creatine 3–5 g/day; omega-3 (EPA/DHA) 1–2 g/day; magnesium glycinate 200–400 mg PM; vitamin D3 1000–2000 IU if needed; iron only if deficient; ginger 1–2 g/day and curcumin 500–1000 mg/day during late luteal/flow if tolerated.
- Menstrual phase (Flow days 1–3): easy-to-digest carbs (oats, rice, ripe fruit), lean proteins (eggs, yogurt, tofu, fish), omega-3s, iron + vitamin C pairing; smaller, more frequent meals; broths/herbal teas; avoid very gassy foods if bloated.
- Early–mid follicular: push carbs around training (pre 30–60 g; post 0.6–0.8 g/kg + 25–40 g protein); varied colorful foods.
- Luteal: stabilize energy; slightly lower carbs 3–4 g/kg unless training heavy; keep protein high; manage cravings with planned snacks; steady electrolytes; 2–3 servings calcium (or fortified alt); limit late caffeine; magnesium for sleep.
- Peri-workout (all phases): if >75–90 min sessions, consider 20–30 g carbs every 30–40 min; post 25–40 g protein + carbs.

- Sleep 7–9 h; consistent schedule. Add 30–60 min during late luteal/flow if fatigued.
- Heat therapy post-session during flow; light mobility helps.
- Strictly avoid Valsalva and jumping on flow days 1–3; use exhale-through-effort and lighter loads.
- Auto-regulate with RPE; if cramps/fatigue elevate RPE, reduce load/sets and favor machines.
- Track symptoms and adjust week-to-week; don’t “make up” missed volume—resume plan.
